learning_e2c0203cba1ebbf5.title: deploy.sh ovh: bsdtar "Refusing to overwrite archive" mid-web-extract leaves service stopped
learning_e2c0203cba1ebbf5.content:
# deploy.sh ovh: bsdtar "Refusing to overwrite archive" mid-web-extract leaves service stopped

2026-04-20 23:27 UTC: `bash deploy.sh ovh` (full mode) failed during Step 3 web-content extract on abydos with: `./Admin/Curator.aspx: Refusing to overwrite archive: No error` then `tar: Error exit delayed from previous errors.`

`set -euo pipefail` at the top of deploy.sh caused the script to abort on the nonzero tar exit — which meant Step 4 (Start service) never ran. **NimbusService was left stopped** because Step 2 had already stopped it. w3wp kept running (IIS untouched), but the legacy TCP listener on :36004 was down and /status publishes stopped.

Root cause hypothesis (unverified): w3wp holds file handles on some .aspx files during extraction. bsdtar (Windows 10+ `tar.exe`) refuses to overwrite a file it thinks might be part of an archive it's currently extracting or processing. Could also be a Windows ACL or SMB file-lock collision with an in-flight IIS request against Curator.aspx.

**Workaround applied:** manual `Start-Service Nimbus` over SSH, then re-ran `bash deploy.sh ovh --service-only --skip-build` which completed cleanly in 60s. Service binaries got updated on the second pass; web content was left partially extracted (NimbusCommon.dll in nimbus-staging/bin was updated, unknown which aspx files did/didn't get extracted).

**How to apply:**
(1) When deploy.sh aborts, IMMEDIATELY SSH abydos and check `Get-Service Nimbus`. If Stopped, restart manually before anything else — legacy TCP clients are down otherwise.
(2) For just getting a service-code fix in place, `--service-only --skip-build` is the safe path (small bundle, no .aspx file-handle contention).
(3) A partial web extract can leave old+new .aspx/DLL mix — track what extracted vs. didn't by comparing LastWriteTime of bin\ files to deploy start time; if suspect, re-run web-only or restore from snapshot.

**Known gap:** deploy.sh should be made more resilient — either retry the tar extraction, or stop w3wp before web extract, or use robocopy with /B flag (backup semantics, bypasses user-level locks). File as backlog if this recurs. Snapshots stored at `C:\temp\rollback\pre_<timestamp>\` on abydos, taken pre-deploy — retain at least 2 generations.

learning_1c4e55e5d7f0eebc.title: SUPERSEDE learning_007: ThreadPool hotfix did NOT hold; premature-victory measurement trap
learning_1c4e55e5d7f0eebc.content:
# SUPERSEDE learning_007: ThreadPool hotfix did NOT hold; premature-victory measurement trap

Correcting `learning_007` from earlier tonight. That learning claimed `ThreadPool.SetMinThreads(128,128)` + MqttHelper 30s timeout (commit fce2e009) fixed the MQTT publish-timeout storm. **The fix did NOT hold.**

Sequence:
- T+0: service restart with hotfix live
- T+26s: 0 err/min, 104 threads → I declared victory
- T+5min: **2483 err/min, 286 threads** → storm fully returned

Why the premature call: I measured before the full v26 fleet (~120 frames) had completed reconnecting. Early in service uptime only ~40 frames had reconnected, threadpool wasn't yet saturated, errors hadn't yet started. Once all ~120 frames were back + handler threads spawned, pool starvation returned. 30s timeout just masks the symptom longer.

Also corrected: I said "~250 v26 frames" in earlier analysis. Actual fleet is ~120 (Tom). Measured thread count 258-286 is ~2× the frame count, which suggests either handler threads don't always exit cleanly on disconnect, or there's >1 thread per connection. Unverified.

**How to apply:**
(1) **When validating a performance fix, measure AFTER the system reaches steady-state load**, not during ramp-up. For NimbusService, steady-state = 5+ minutes after restart when the full v26 TCP fleet has finished reconnecting. 30-second post-restart measurements are worthless.
(2) `ThreadPool.SetMinThreads(128,128)` alone is not sufficient when legacy thread-per-connection I/O holds ~120+ dedicated threads that compete with pool threads for CPU. The floor doesn't address the contention.
(3) The proper fix remains `backlog_fbfaa7381046` — replace thread-per-connection TCP handler with async I/O in `picFrameServer.cs`. Threads would drop from 250+ to ~16.
(4) Interim mitigation that does NOT require code-path rework: **downgrade `MqttHelper.cs` line 210/233 log levels from ERR → WRN** (for TimeoutException specifically), and add rate-limited per-minute aggregation line. Stops Grafana alert noise without pretending to fix the underlying. 10-15 min of code, zero deploy risk. Parked awaiting coordinator/Tom routing decision.

Hotfix commit `fce2e009` is still live on abydos. Net-neutral vs pre-fix state; no reason to roll back. Rollback snapshot at `C:\temp\rollback\pre_20260420T2305\` if needed.

learning_1278cde388acb626.title: az vm CLI has a known bug on VMs with secretsManagementSettings — use az rest REST API instead
learning_1278cde388acb626.content:
# az vm CLI has a known bug on VMs with secretsManagementSettings — use az rest REST API instead

Hit 2026-04-20 multiple times. Commands like `az vm get-instance-view`, `az vm list --show-details`, `az vm list -d`, and some other `az vm` subcommands fail with:

```
AAZInvalidValueError: Expect <class 'dict'>, got secretsManagementSettings (<class 'str'>)
```

This is an azure-cli 2.x parser bug when VMs have certain properties set (specifically `secretsManagementSettings` as a string in the newer Azure API payload). Affects `nimbus-staging-west-vm` in nimbus-prod-westus-rg, possibly others.

**Workaround:** Use the direct REST API via `az rest`:
```bash
az rest --method get --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/15cacff5-4727-4aa4-b6cf-652724e44a7c/resourceGroups/nimbus-prod-westus-rg/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/<VM_NAME>/instanceView?api-version=2024-07-01" --query "statuses[?starts_with(code,'PowerState')].displayStatus" -o tsv
```

Returns "VM running", "VM deallocated", etc. Works for ALL vm instance-view queries the broken CLI can't do. Note: `az vm deallocate`, `az vm start`, `az vm stop`, `az vm resize` themselves still work — the bug is only on reading extended instance view.

learning_4413739fc3425180.title: Always git diff before git add on files with pre-existing working-tree drift
learning_4413739fc3425180.content:
# Always git diff before git add on files with pre-existing working-tree drift

When starting a session, `git status` may show files already modified by prior sessions (e.g., Web.config was already "M" at the start of this session with an unrelated in-progress Meilisearch IP change). When you then edit one of those files for a different reason and `git add <path>`, git stages ALL pending changes to that file — sweeping prior drift into your commit.

Incident: commit 51950f79 was intended to be KV-cleanup only. It also swept up `Meilisearch:Host=http://10.0.4.4:7700` → `http://10.100.0.1:7700` (Azure VNet IP → stargate WG IP) drift from a prior session. The change itself was correct (matches setup-ovh-webconfig.sh convention and deployed state), so no harm — but the commit description didn't mention it, which is a history-integrity failure.

Rule: before `git add path/file`, run `git diff path/file` (not just `git diff --stat`) to see all pending changes. If drift is unrelated to your task, stash it or commit it separately with its own explanation. Don't let unrelated changes hide in a named commit.

Alternative: use `git add -p` to interactively stage only the hunks you intend. Safer default when any working-tree drift exists at session start.

Applies especially at `go` time: the carry-over from prior sessions is often partial work. Treat every "M" file in `git status` as a known hazard, not as your own in-progress work.

learning_6ce936c533ba56b5.title: NimbusWatchdog is now decoupled from NimbusCommon — edit coupling note if FrameDetails schema changes
learning_6ce936c533ba56b5.content:
# NimbusWatchdog is now decoupled from NimbusCommon — edit coupling note if FrameDetails schema changes

As of commit bfc6d6b1, NimbusWatchdog no longer ProjectReferences NimbusCommon. NimbusCommon targets net472; watchdog targets net8.0 and needs to publish cross-platform (likely linux/stargate).

Watchdog reads `frame:{id}:data` Redis blobs as raw JObject instead of deserializing to NimbusCommon/InterfaceData.FrameDetails. Field names are hard-referenced by string in `RedisMaintenance.CleanupStaleDeviceStatuses`:
- "OnlineStatus"
- "Temp"
- "Unique"

If server-side code (picFrameWeb or NimbusService) ever renames any of those fields in FrameDetails, **NimbusWatchdog will silently stop evicting stale frames** (JObject access returns null for unknown fields, so `onlineStatus == "offline"` short-circuits and nothing gets flipped). There's no compile-time safety — the coupling is by string.

Mitigations in place:
- A coupling note at `RedisMaintenance.cs:13` explaining the hard-coded field names.
- Per-sweep log line `"Sweep done: scanned=X evicted=Y dead_servers=[...]"` so operators can see if evictions dropped to zero (which would hint at a schema mismatch).

If you're renaming frame-detail fields, grep NimbusWatchdog for the old name too.

learning_6d6000086e2d1d78.title: Redis history mediaType:-1 is server-side dual-write artifact, not frame failure
learning_6d6000086e2d1d78.content:
# Redis history mediaType:-1 is server-side dual-write artifact, not frame failure

Mike 518 investigation 2026-04-20/21 (frames-team):

**SYMPTOM:** Redis frame:{uuid}:data History array shows every entry with mediaType:-1 (interpreted by runbook as "playback error"). Looks like frame is failing every image.

**FINDING:** The frame is NOT failing. picFrameClient only broadcasts `imageChange` with `mediaType:0` — this is the ONLY mediaType the frame itself ever emits. Server-side writes a second history entry ~0.2-0.6s later with mediaType:-1 for the SAME id. Both writes land in History, so the array contains pairs of (mediaType:0, mediaType:-1) for the same image id.

**EVIDENCE:**
- Mike 518 picFrame.log 00:48-01:00 UTC 2026-04-21: every cycle shows clean sequence — `MediaManager playImage`, `JavaFX playing X srcfile:...jpg`, `image presented at...`, `Broadcast imageChange mediaType:0`. No -1 ever broadcast. Watchdog threads all healthy.
- Transient `MediaPlayList.java:377 - got null media for return` warnings are retry noise that succeeds — not related.
- JPEG files on disk match mdf target dimensions exactly (810x1080 mdf = 810x1080 on disk for img 92459, same for 30942, 87879, 90179, 62794). Server-team 3cfbf68f MediaLayout.scale fix is working correctly.
- Redis History timestamps always show mediaType:-1 entry with later playTime than the paired mediaType:0 entry.

**LIKELY SERVER-SIDE ROOT CAUSE:** Per learning_c2ef6544c825dc90 (2026-04-13), the History array is written from TWO paths: setCurrentMedia (PicFrame.cs:1861) AND MqttStatusHandler. One path resolves the Image record successfully → mediaType:0. A second path fails to resolve OR gets ContentType=0 but mediaType missing from the source object → writes -1. The -1 write lands second, so it's the visible "latest" entry in the History array.

**SCOPE DISCIPLINE:** This is NOT a frames-team bug. picFrameClient's only job is to broadcast imageChange; it does so correctly with mediaType:0. Investigation must go to server-team.

**USER IMPACT:** Zero. Frames display correctly. The only visible symptom is the admin page's "last 10 played" showing mediaType:-1 for everything.

**FOR FUTURE DEBUGGING:** If Redis history shows mediaType:-1 on a 26.x legacy frame, verify by (1) reading the picFrame.log imageChange broadcasts — if they show mediaType:0, the frame is fine, (2) checking if on-disk JPEGs and mdf sizes match. If both check out, the issue is observability-layer only and does not require a frame fix.

learning_2bff9935e8c271ea.title: MqttHelper publish timeout was DOUBLE-logging: catch-all (line 238) re-logged the thrown TimeoutException
learning_2bff9935e8c271ea.content:
# MqttHelper publish timeout was DOUBLE-logging: catch-all (line 238) re-logged the thrown TimeoutException

# The storm was inflated by a double-log bug, not just raw timeout rate

Before commit 28b4c7b3, `MqttHelper.PublishAsync` on timeout did:
1. `log.Error("MQTT publish timeout after 30s to topic...")` at line 215
2. `throw new TimeoutException(...)` at line 216
3. Caught by the `catch (Exception ex)` catch-all at line 236
4. Which **logged ERR AGAIN** at line 238 with message like "MQTT unexpected error during publish... TimeoutException - MQTT publish timed out"

So every publish timeout produced **two** ERR lines, not one. The 2500/min storm was really ~1250/min real timeouts, double-logged.

The fix in 28b4c7b3 replaces `throw` with `return` on the timeout branch. Since the catch-all at 238 was already swallowing the throw (not rethrowing), caller-visible behavior is unchanged — callers of `PublishAsync` already saw the method return normally on timeout. The double-log is just removed.

**Implication for option 5 scoping:** raw timeout rate on the hot-path is ~1250-1750/min (per aggregator samples 18:38-18:42 UTC 2026-04-21 showing 1281-1745), not 2500-3000/min as state-spec and earlier diagnostics suggested. Thread-pool starvation analysis should use the corrected rate.

Subscribe path (line 276) has the same ERR log but the throw was not double-caught — SubscribeAsync has no try/catch wrapping its body, the TimeoutException propagates to the caller. So fix there was count + stash, keep throw.

learning_8ef8f52257af24f1.title: Grafana alert nimbus-error-cutover uses !~ exclusions, NOT |~ requires — downgrading ERR→WRN never breaks it
learning_8ef8f52257af24f1.content:
# Grafana alert nimbus-error-cutover uses !~ exclusions, NOT |~ requires — downgrading ERR→WRN never breaks it

# Before changing log levels in server code, check how Grafana consumes them

The cutover-watch alert at `infra/stargate/grafana/nimbus-alert-rules.yaml:41` uses Loki LogQL:

```
count_over_time({app="nimbus"} | json | level="error" !~ `getImage.ashx` !~ `previewing deletion` !~ `Rank` !~ `getWebImageAsStream` !~ `LogPersistenceService` [5m])
```

- `level="error"` hard-filters to ERR only.
- `!~` patterns are exclusions — they REDUCE the count.
- No `|~` (require) patterns — nothing depends on a specific ERR string existing.

So downgrading any specific ERR log to WRN is always a pure alert-noise improvement. It will never break a paging rule.

**General principle:** before downgrading log levels in C#, grep the Grafana alerts file (`infra/stargate/grafana/nimbus-alert-rules.yaml`) for the message text or logger name. If there's a `|~ 'your_text'` clause, you break that alert. If there's only `!~` exclusions or no mention, you're safe.

Relevant when coordinator asks "check Grafana before downgrading log level" — the answer is almost always "safe" unless the exclusion list specifically includes the same text (which would indicate the alert was already papering over it and should be cleaned up in the same commit).

learning_49e46d64105a2c70.title: PicFrame TCP handler is thread-per-connection: 2 dedicated threads per frame + BeginRead callbacks
learning_49e46d64105a2c70.content:
# PicFrame TCP handler is thread-per-connection: 2 dedicated threads per frame + BeginRead callbacks

# Why the MqttHelper storm causes thread-pool starvation

`picFrameServer.cs:167 AcceptSSLCallback` → `new PicFrame(stream, handler)` → `PicFrame.init()` (PicFrame.cs:184) spawns **two dedicated threads per connection**:

- `sendThread` running `SendThreadProcess` (writes to socket)
- `recvThread` running `ProcessRead` (processes bufferList)
- Plus `BeginRead` AsyncCallback into `SSLStreamReceiveCallback` which runs on thread-pool

With ~120 legacy v26 frames active on abydos, that's roughly **240 long-lived per-connection threads** plus intermittent pool usage for SSL callback and MQTT ACK continuations.

Inside PicFrame.cs there are **49 sync-blocking calls** (`.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` / `.Wait()`) on async operations including MQTT publishes, database queries, and artwork repo calls. Each of these blocks a per-connection thread for up to 30s (the MQTT publish timeout) during storm conditions.

This is the root-cause architecture of the TP starvation note in `MqttHelper.cs:19-23` ("ThreadPool starvation in NimbusService, 222 threads in ExecutionDelay, queue length 163/sec"). The SetMinThreads(128,128) + 30s timeout (commit fce2e009) was a band-aid.

**Scope implication:** Rewriting PicFrame.cs handler from thread-per-connection to Task-based would touch all 49 sync sites + ServerConnection.cs (920 lines, similar pattern). ~2-4 focused sessions minimum. HIGH regression risk because reply-correlation (PicFrame.cs:1747 `_replyMqtt.Value.PublishAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult()`) and event ordering (status/online → status → changed sequence) cannot be reordered or dropped.

**Strategic implication:** This code is depreciating as v27 frames replace v26 — v27 uses MQTT-native, no TCP path. Don't invest engineering in the thread-per-conn rewrite; fix the fragility in the shared `MqttHelper` core instead (Phase A: MQTTnet CT upgrade), which benefits both legacy and v27.

learning_c750a3a5ba41ab2e.title: Legacy frame SD cards have A/B-root layout with empty spare p3 — migration flip is one cmdline line
learning_c750a3a5ba41ab2e.content:
# Legacy frame SD cards have A/B-root layout with empty spare p3 — migration flip is one cmdline line

Verified 2026-04-21 by SSH to frame 26 (192.168.15.212, hostname "art", Pi 3B Rev 1.2, Raspbian 8 Jessie, root key id_nimbusframe_root).

Legacy SD card partition table (same on all legacy frames per Tom):
- p1: 63 MB FAT32 boot (/boot) — contains cmdline.txt, config.txt, Pi firmware
- p2: 3.2 GB ext4 — active rootfs (/)
- p3: 3.2 GB ext4 — SPARE, unmounted, contents = lost+found + stale "System Volume Information" dir from 2017. 5.7 MB used of 3.2 GB. Identical size to p2.
- p4: 23.3 GB ext4 — data partition (/usr/local/bin). Holds JDK (jdk_8-132.gz), picFrame.jar, picFrameStart.jar, scripts, images. Mounted regardless of which root is active.

Migration mechanism is literally:
1. Stage v27 rootfs (Trixie base) onto p3 via tar extract or dd
2. Deposit Liberica JDK 17 Full + new picFrame.jar onto /usr/local/bin (coexists with v26 JDK 8)
3. Edit /boot/cmdline.txt: `root=/dev/mmcblk0p2` -> `root=/dev/mmcblk0p3`
4. Reboot
5. Rollback: flip cmdline.txt back to p2, reboot. Trivial.

Implications:
- Customer SD-card swap is NOT required for migration. Remote in-place migration is viable.
- v27 rootfs doesn't need to bundle JDK (shared p4 data partition handles it).
- 3.2 GB is plenty for Trixie base without JDK.
- Rollback is boot-level, one file edit. Watchdog can implement boot-once-validate-then-commit by having the new rootfs's first-boot script flip cmdline.txt back to p2 if app heartbeat doesn't arrive within N minutes.

Caveats / risks still open:
- v27 frame-mode has never run standalone anywhere. PicFrameLauncher INCOMPLETE.
- Pi 3B has 735 MB RAM. Trixie + Liberica JDK 17 Full + JavaFX Monocle under sustained load may OOM. Never tested on Pi 3B (bench has been Pi Zero 2W bridges).
- Fleet hardware variance not audited. Pi 1 / Pi 2 / Pi Zero in the fleet physically can't run v27.
- Legacy launcher is rsync-only (learning_970). Migration payload fanout requires rsync OTA endpoint on stargate (currently deferred) or frame-by-frame CallHome SSH push.
- Boot-once-validate-then-commit watchdog not written yet. Standard initramfs hook pattern, ~1 week work including soak.

Supersedes my earlier worry (in msg_afc23a87617a to coordinator) that legacy cards might have no spare partition. They do. Partition flip is cheap. The remaining expensive work is frame-mode code completion + Pi 3B RAM verification + hardware-variance audit + boot-commit watchdog.

learning_28fe3d8e4d3f3658.title: OnlineFrames is NOT a SQL table (in Azure or MySQL) — it is in-memory dict + Redis state
learning_28fe3d8e4d3f3658.content:
# OnlineFrames is NOT a SQL table (in Azure or MySQL) — it is in-memory dict + Redis state

2026-04-21 — Verified via grep across nimbus-server codebase and DATABASE_SCHEMA.md (Azure SQL source of truth) + stargate MySQL information_schema: **no object named OnlineFrames exists in any database schema, current or historical.**

The name `OnlineFrames` / `onlineFrames` in the codebase refers to:
1. **In-memory dict**: `Nimbus.onlineFrames` — a `ConcurrentDictionary<string, FrameInfo>` on each NimbusService process, tracking currently TCP-connected legacy frames. (picFrameServiceLibrary/Nimbus.cs)
2. **WCF method**: `INimbus.getOnlineFrames()` — returns the dict as JSON across process boundary (NimbusService → picFrameWeb). (picFrameServiceLibrary/INimbus.cs:40)
3. **Redis-scanning cleanup**: `ClearStaleOnlineFrames()` (Nimbus.cs:1137) — scans Redis keys `frame:*:data`, clears `FrameDetails.OnlineStatus` field for this server on service startup. Does NOT touch SQL.

**Sources of truth for online-ness, in order of authority:**
- TCP ESTABLISHED socket count on :36004 (hard evidence)
- In-memory `Nimbus.onlineFrames` dict (NimbusService live state)
- Redis `frame:{uuid}:data.OnlineStatus` field (persisted shortly after connect/disconnect)
- `Frames.LastConnection` column — coarser proxy, stamped on fresh TCP connect only, not per-heartbeat

Any "recently online frame count" query should use Redis scan or TCP netstat, not a SQL table.

**Supersedes my earlier learning learning_5c9 which incorrectly characterized this as a NimbusSync migration gap.** There is nothing to migrate — the object never existed as a database artifact.

learning_530c46ce706890b3.title: T-SQL leftovers in Dapper migration: scan for @@ROWCOUNT, @@IDENTITY, TOP n, ISNULL, NOLOCK hints
learning_530c46ce706890b3.content:
# T-SQL leftovers in Dapper migration: scan for @@ROWCOUNT, @@IDENTITY, TOP n, ISNULL, NOLOCK hints

2026-04-21 — Found that `ImageLayoutRepository.SetLayoutAsync` contained SQL Server T-SQL (`IF @@ROWCOUNT = 0 INSERT`) that silently broke every first-time non-Art image layout save on OVH post-cutover. Error 1064 at parse time means the UPDATE didn't execute either — MySQL rejects the whole command. User 2181's image 97372 was the report; the bug was fleet-wide for anyone trying to crop a newly-uploaded image.

Grep across the whole nimbus-server repo for the pattern found only ONE occurrence of `@@ROWCOUNT`. But T-SQL contamination during the Dapper migration is a pattern worth scanning for proactively. Suggested scan patterns (all can be run with `Grep` tool against *.cs):
- `@@ROWCOUNT` — SQL Server only (MySQL uses `ROW_COUNT()`)
- `@@IDENTITY` — SQL Server last-insert-id (MySQL uses `LAST_INSERT_ID()`)
- `SCOPE_IDENTITY()` — SQL Server only
- `SELECT TOP \d+` — SQL Server (MySQL uses `LIMIT`)
- `ISNULL\(` — both exist but differ; MySQL's is `IFNULL()` / `COALESCE()`
- `WITH \(NOLOCK\)` — SQL Server hint, invalid MySQL
- `NEWID\(\)` — SQL Server (MySQL uses `UUID()`)
- `GETDATE\(\)` — SQL Server (MySQL uses `NOW()` / `UTC_TIMESTAMP()`)
- `IF @@[A-Z]+ =|IF EXISTS\s*\(` outside stored procs — T-SQL control flow that needs rewrite as DELIMITER-bounded routine or separate queries

Fix pattern for upserts on MySQL: `INSERT ... VALUES ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE col = VALUES(col)`. Requires a PK or UNIQUE constraint on the conflict column.

Fix applied in commit d9b03355 (master). Deployed to abydos 2026-04-21. Verified upsert works via direct MySQL query.

**Lesson:** When migrating repository methods from T-SQL to MySQL, a single green build does not mean the query runs. Build-time checks catch C# errors but NOT SQL dialect mismatches, which only surface at first execution. Integration-test every mutating query or accept that post-cutover breakage is likely.

learning_ef4ce41b76c7a788.content:
# v27 bridge OTA polling visibility via stargate nginx — and bridge-588-class wedge pattern

Discovered 2026-04-21 while diagnosing why bridge 588 (Ron) hadn't upgraded to agent 1.15.4.

Source of truth for "is this bridge polling OTA": /var/log/nginx/frames.access.log on stargate (NOT the main access.log — that's port-80 scanner noise). Look for GET /api/updates/index?serial=<CpuId>. User-Agent "Go-http-client/2.0" identifies nimbus-agent. Each agent has a consistent per-hour minute:second pattern (e.g. hh:21:11 for one bridge, hh:55:39 for another).

Fleet finding 2026-04-21: only 2 of 14 v27 bridges in the fleet were polling OTA. HwIds 586 and 589 — both bridge_Normal, both upgraded cleanly to 1.15.4. Other 12 bridges silent. Specifically bridge 588 (Ron, CpuId 0000000064d4cc3b) had ZERO /api/updates/index hits in 4+ days of log.

Pattern signature of "OTA goroutine dead, MQTT alive":
- Bridges.LastConnection current (MQTT heartbeat still firing, from BridgeHandler.StartStatusLoop)
- Bridges.Version stuck at pre-bump value
- Bridges.UpdatedAt tracks LastConnection (updated by heartbeat path)
- Nginx frames.access.log shows zero /api/updates/index hits from bridge's serial
- Meural frames under the bridge may also be dead-classloader but that's a separate class

How to tell from the dashboard side: agent version field in Bridges table has been stable for days while the ConfigGroups target moved. If more than one hour has passed since ConfigGroups bump and a bridge's Version doesn't match, it's either wedged or not-polling-for-network-reasons.

Matches learning_6f1 class (silent goroutine death from bufio scanner buffer bug, fixed in 1.15.1). 1.13.2 predates the fix, so Ron's bridge is vulnerable to the same class.

1.15.6 adds an OTA watchdog that self-restarts the agent if check() hasn't fired in >3h. Post-1.15.6 fleet-wide rollout, this class of wedge becomes self-healing. Pre-rollout bridges still need manual restart/reboot.

Bootstrap limitation: if a bridge is wedged on 1.13.2, it can't receive 1.15.6. Ron's bridge 588 will only recover when he reboots.

Operational takeaway: weekly fleet check should include diffing ConfigGroups.AgentVersion vs Bridges.Version by group and flagging any bridges behind for more than 2h. A simple cron on stargate that does this query and pages coordinator on drift would catch these early.

Also noticed: HwIds 554, 567, 572 report agent Version="27.1.0" — that's a picFrame version leaking into the agent field. Latent field-mapping bug, low priority, worth fixing in a future release.

learning_6601ec9f168544dd.title: ASP.NET WebForms namespaces client IDs — regex matching server-rendered control IDs must anchor at end or use endswith
learning_6601ec9f168544dd.content:
# ASP.NET WebForms namespaces client IDs — regex matching server-rendered control IDs must anchor at end or use endswith

2026-04-21 — Cost me 2 deploys + LAYDIAG diagnostic to identify.

Server-side setupFrameTypes in EditLayout.aspx.cs does `cb.ID = "cb" + row.Id`. When ASP.NET renders the page, the NamingContainer prefix is prepended to every rendered client id: the browser sees `id="ctl00_ContentPlaceHolder1_cb26"`, not `id="cb26"`.

Client-side JS built `checkedFrames` via `parseInt(this.id.replace('cb',''))`. For a namespaced id this yields NaN → JSON.stringify emits null → DeserializeObject<List<int>> throws at the server. I fixed that initial crash with a strict regex `/^cb(\d+)$/` — but that regex ALSO excluded the legitimate namespaced IDs, so checkedFrameIds silently came through as `[]` and the per-frame save branch iterated zero times.

**Correct regex for matching an ASP.NET-rendered server control id:** `/(?:^|_)cb(\d+)$/`.

Rule of thumb: whenever a JS selector queries rendered control ids, either (a) prefer ASP.NET-provided `<%= Control.ClientID %>` strings as exact-match anchors, or (b) regex-match the *suffix* not the start of the id. The `_` underscore is the path separator.

Same class of bug is likely lurking in other .aspx + .js pairs that use heuristic string stripping on client ids — anywhere we see `this.id.replace('prefix','')` is suspect.

Commit df7b3183 has the fix.

learning_29a5d5a1fe855de4.title: nimbus-agent Docker build silently produces binaries with version="0.1.0" — caused fleet OTA download loop 2026-04-21
learning_29a5d5a1fe855de4.content:
# nimbus-agent Docker build silently produces binaries with version="0.1.0" — caused fleet OTA download loop 2026-04-21

Dockerfile.build previously ran `git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo "0.1.0"` INSIDE the build container, after `COPY . .`. Build context is nimbus-agent/ subdirectory which has no .git (that lives at raspframe/.git one level up). `git describe` silently errors, `|| echo "0.1.0"` fallback kicks in, binary is built with `main.version="0.1.0"` while the filename on stargate is `nimbus-agent.<tag>` and the manifest advertises the correct version.

Failure mode: ota.Updater.check() at updater.go:277 compares manifest comp.Version to the running u.agentVersion (set from main.version at build via ldflags). Mismatch → re-download → install → systemd restart → same process repeats every ~2 minutes (startup+2min initial OTA check cadence). Each restart also kills and respawns Meural JVM children.

Concrete incident 2026-04-21: frames-team shipped 1.15.6 this way. Tom bumped ConfigGroups.AgentVersion to 1.15.6 on Init/Normal/Alpha. Bridges 586 and 589 downloaded 1.15.6 and entered the loop — 589 downloaded nimbus-agent.1.15.6 (9.4 MB) every ~2 min for roughly 8 cycles before rollback. 587 was offline so escaped. Tom rolled bridge_Normal to 1.15.4, then Init/Alpha to 1.15.4, stopping the loop.

Root of silent failure: bash || fallback swallowed the git error with zero log output. Binary ran fine, MQTT fine, nginx manifest fine — every layer green except the binary's self-reported version string.

Fix in commit bd23d76 (2026-04-21): Dockerfile.build removed in-container git describe; accepts ARG VERSION as build-arg; hard-fails if VERSION is left at "0.0.0-dev" sentinel. Makefile build-arm target now passes --build-arg VERSION=$(VERSION) where VERSION is git describe on HOST. Frames-team MUST grep new binaries for literal version string before uploading: `grep -ao -E '1\.15\.[0-9]+|0\.1\.0' nimbus-agent-X.Y.Z | sort -u`.

Note: previously-shipped 1.15.5 binary on stargate has the same defect but never caused a loop because ConfigGroups was never pointed at it (went 1.15.4 → 1.15.6 directly). Pending Tom's decision on deletion vs rebuild. Low risk as long as AgentVersion never gets set to "1.15.5".

Operational rule going forward: the build pipeline must NEVER produce a binary whose embedded version disagrees with its filename. The fail-fast guard makes this a hard-stop at build time.

learning_b96ea49f5ccf2e24.title: Storage write-activity scans: use `az monitor metrics list Transactions` by ApiName, not `az storage blob list`
learning_b96ea49f5ccf2e24.content:
# Storage write-activity scans: use `az monitor metrics list Transactions` by ApiName, not `az storage blob list`

**Fact:** For "is this storage account still being written to post-cutover?" questions, listing all blobs doesn't scale (580 GB / 680k files ≈ hours to enumerate, OOM risk, expensive CLI calls) and JMESPath `lastModified` filters are client-side post-filter — pagination brings back everything first.

The right tool is `az monitor metrics list` against the storage account with metric=`Transactions`, filtered by `ApiName`. Returns aggregate transaction counts per time interval per API. Free, fast (~2s), and directly answers "is there any write-type activity."

**Key API names to filter on for real writes:**
- `PutBlob`, `PutBlock`, `PutBlockList`, `AppendBlock` — create/append
- `CopyBlob` — copy
- `SetBlobProperties`, `SetBlobMetadata` — mutations
- `DeleteBlob` — deletes (include if cleanup activity counts, exclude for "is user data still being written")

**Critical gotcha — AppendBlock is usually noise:** Azure Storage Analytics writes diagnostic logs as append-blobs into `$logs` container, which shows as heavy `AppendBlock` activity indistinguishable from real user appending. Distinguish real user writes by filtering OUT `AppendBlock` (or breaking down per API).

On 2026-04-21 I found `nimbus` account: ~5000 AppendBlock/day (all noise — $logs diagnostics) + 36 real PutBlob/day (the actual per-day user delta). Without the per-API breakdown I would've thought the account was actively used when it's essentially dormant except for internal telemetry.

**Command template:**
```bash
az monitor metrics list --resource <acct> --resource-group <rg> \
  --resource-type "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts" \
  --metric "Transactions" \
  --filter "ApiName eq 'PutBlob' or ApiName eq 'PutBlock' or ApiName eq 'PutBlockList' or ApiName eq 'CopyBlob'" \
  --start-time 2026-04-17T00:00:00Z --interval P1D --aggregation Total \
  --query "value[0].timeseries[0].data[].{day:timeStamp, writes:total}" -o tsv
```

**Also note:** `az storage blob list --auth-mode login` fails on this subscription (management-plane owner doesn't auto-get data-plane RBAC). Use `--auth-mode key` with a fetched account key: `az storage account keys list --account-name X -g Y --query "[0].value" -o tsv`.

**Correct casing trap:** `az disk show/list` uses `diskSizeGB` (uppercase GB), not `diskSizeGb`. Lowercase returns `None` silently.

learning_39e30066ae99a5d6.title: nimbus-agent startup-before-network wedge on bridge 587 (2026-04-21) — CloudMQTT + OTA give up after first failure, no retry
learning_39e30066ae99a5d6.content:
# nimbus-agent startup-before-network wedge on bridge 587 (2026-04-21) — CloudMQTT + OTA give up after first failure, no retry

Discovered 2026-04-21 ~17:20 CDT investigating bridge 587 (HwId 587, UUID dc5ae9bf-115a-4135-b161-7726535bf6a8, card now in .47 after Tom's WiFi recovery). Bridge was WiFi-connected and reachable over SSH, but Bridges.LastConnection in DB stuck at 2026-04-19 12:55. Agent (1.15.3) had been running 10h with zero cloud activity in journal — only BLE traffic.

Root cause: agent started at 07:00:27 CDT BEFORE WiFi DHCP completed (WiFi "connected to LemmonsLakeHouse" logged at 07:33:55, 33 minutes AFTER agent started). At startup, /etc/resolv.conf wasn't yet populated by NetworkManager/systemd-resolved. Agent's cloud MQTT connect + 2-minute OTA check both failed with:

  dial tcp: lookup frames.nimbusframe.net on [::1]:53: read udp [::1]:<port>->[::1]:53: read: connection refused

The [::1]:53 = Go resolver falling back to IPv6 localhost when /etc/resolv.conf is empty. "connection refused" = nothing listening (systemd-resolved stub not yet running or not reachable).

The critical bug: CloudMQTT logged "(will retry in background)" but apparently did NOT retry. OTA logged failure and then silence for 10+ hours. Paho MQTT client's AutoReconnect behavior either isn't configured on our CloudClient OR was defeated by the initial DNS-failure error class. OTA's hourly ticker also appears dead after the first failed check.

Current network state on .47 at 17:20 CDT: DNS resolves (51.81.243.11), ping works, HTTPS 443 returns 405 (server alive), MQTT 8883 TCP-open — network is fine. Agent just never retried.

**Fix for bridge 587 right now**: `systemctl restart nimbus-agent`. Agent restarts with working DNS, cloud MQTT + OTA succeed, and picks up 1.15.4 OTA (bridge_Alpha is at 1.15.4).

**Design error found in 1.15.6 watchdog**: it's scoped to 3h, which makes sense for silent-goroutine-death mid-operation (bridge 588 class) but is WRONG for startup-race (bridge 587 class). Tom called this out correctly: 3h is absurd for "just booted, DNS was briefly not ready."

**Right design for 1.15.7+**: (a) proper auto-reconnect with exponential backoff in CloudMQTT client and OTA updater, (b) pre-flight DNS check before attempting cloud operations, (c) structured state reporting to local/agent/cloudState ("waiting-for-network" vs "cloud-unreachable" vs "connected"), (d) systemd unit After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target to prevent early-start in the first place, (e) KEEP 3h watchdog but only as last-resort safety net when the retry loop itself has gone silent.

Prevention story (systemd ordering) + fast-recovery story (backoff reconnect) + safety-net story (3h watchdog) — three distinct layers, each appropriate for its failure class.

Affects: all bridges that experience a slow DHCP/network-online event at boot. Anything on an SD card where the agent starts faster than the WiFi supplicant completes association, which is common on first boot after a card swap or cold power-on.

learning_8d32f44eb49b6422.title: Managed-disk SAS azcopy transfers the full VHD, not sparse-compressed
learning_8d32f44eb49b6422.content:
# Managed-disk SAS azcopy transfers the full VHD, not sparse-compressed

When using `az disk grant-access` + `azcopy copy` to pull a managed disk as a VHD, azcopy streams the full logical size (for a 127 GB disk: 136,367,309,312 bytes exactly = 127.0 GiB including the VHD footer). It does NOT skip zeroed/unallocated blocks, unlike typical dynamic-VHD file transfers from on-prem Hyper-V or from Azure unmanaged VHD blobs where sparse blocks compress to 30-80% of nominal size. Plan managed-disk captures for the FULL disk size: (a) local free space, (b) egress cost (~$0.087/GB West US), (c) wall time — 127 GiB at ~40 MB/s disk-limited write is ~55 min. Staging2 capture 2026-04-21 confirmed: azcopy job summary showed "Total Number of Bytes Transferred: 136367309312" vs azure's estimate of 30-80 GB in msg_1b97cc2865f7.

learning_7d4fdd692a893cf2.title: az disk grant-access returns accessSAS (uppercase), not accessSas — JMESPath is case-sensitive
learning_7d4fdd692a893cf2.content:
# az disk grant-access returns accessSAS (uppercase), not accessSas — JMESPath is case-sensitive

`az disk grant-access ... --query accessSas -o tsv` returns an empty string on az CLI 2.85, silently — the actual JSON property is `accessSAS`. JMESPath matching is case-sensitive. This is a common copy-paste bug because Microsoft docs historically used both casings. Correct command: `az disk grant-access -g <rg> -n <disk> --access-level Read --duration-in-seconds 28800 --query accessSAS -o tsv`. Verify the returned SAS is non-empty before piping to azcopy. If you run azcopy with an empty source URL, you'll get a confusing URL-parsing error far from the actual root cause.

learning_4c38dfcee52d17fb.title: Coordinator pattern: assertion-before-verification is a reliable error source
learning_4c38dfcee52d17fb.content:
# Coordinator pattern: assertion-before-verification is a reliable error source

Pattern I committed this session and Tom caught explicitly:

Said "storm is executing tonight regardless" after dispatching msg_b83673f2817b + msg_af25329bbc89 to storm. Treated the dispatch being queued as equivalent to the work happening. It was not — Tom had parked storm, messages sat unread.

Also: said "we probably have zero VHDs" without checking the actual state of `/e/NimbusAzureBackup/disks/` or asking storm's state spec. Tom's "we have one vhd, that is good" was the correct state (storm completed staging2 VHD capture before park; 127 GiB landed). My doubt contradicted both observable state and Tom's statement.

Rule for future coordinator work:
1. A dispatched message is a task-queued event, NOT a task-in-progress event. Do not describe it as "executing" or "in-flight" until you have confirmation the recipient agent is active and has acknowledged or begun work.
2. Before asserting state about an external agent's work (especially stopped/completed/not-done), verify via memory_list_agents or memory_get_active_work or the agent's state spec. "I think X is happening" is worse than "I don't know, let me check."
3. When the user states an outcome you haven't verified, do not contradict reflexively. Verify first. If they're wrong, the data will tell you. If they're right, you would have caused unnecessary friction.
4. "Anti-sycophancy" rule doesn't mean "treat user statements as suspect." It means accuracy over agreement. Accuracy sometimes means trusting the user over your own unverified assumptions.

Corrective work in this session: sent msg_0444d38f98f1 correcting my prior wrong assertion about VHD status to azure; re-sent capture-cancel to storm; acknowledged error to Tom directly.

This is a behavioral learning, not a codebase fact. File under coordinator-discipline for future coordinator sessions to read during startup.

learning_f61f59be499ddf67.title: Per-Meural identity MUST be in frame_config.json only — forking caused bridge-587 register-429 loop
learning_f61f59be499ddf67.content:
# Per-Meural identity MUST be in frame_config.json only — forking caused bridge-587 register-429 loop

## The rule

The only on-disk source of truth for a Meural's identity (UUID, name, IP, serial, MQTT creds) is `meurals/{uuid}/frame_config.json`. Do not introduce a second file that duplicates any identity field. See `spec:bridge-per-meural-persistence` for the authoritative layout.

## Why (concrete incident, 2026-04-21)

Before 1.15.7, Meural identity was forked:
- `saveMeuralConfig` (meural/commands.go) wrote `meural.json` with `id/name/ip/serialNumber/mqttUsername/mqttPassword`.
- `writeMeuralConfig` (supervisor/supervisor.go) wrote `frame_config.json` with `unique/serverUrl/mqttUsername/mqttPassword/mqttBroker`.
- `LoadMeuralConfigs` read `meural.json`. Anything without a `meural.json` on disk was invisible to the agent.

Bridge 587 ended up in this state (either because `meural.json` was never written on that bridge's earlier pairing, or it got removed). Effect:

1. Agent starts, `LoadMeuralConfigs` returns zero Meurals.
2. Cloud MQTT delivers bridge config listing two Meurals.
3. `reconcileMeurals` sees "in config but not running" for both → calls `/api/device/register` for each.
4. Server returns 429 (cpuSerial already registered).
5. Retry on every config receive → permanent loop, Alpha ConfigGroup 1.15.6 broken on any bridge with legacy disk layout.

Took ~4 hours overnight to root-cause. The fix (collapse to frame_config.json) is 30 LOC; the damage was architectural.

## Prevention rules (applied in 1.15.7)

1. One file per concern. If two pieces of code need the same data, they read the same file.
2. `LoadMeuralConfigs` and `WriteMeuralConfig` MUST operate on the same file. Any future refactor that splits read/write paths must update both or neither.
3. Any new identity field goes into `frame_config.json` + update the spec. Do not invent a second file.
4. The Java side has hard-coded readers for `HWconfig.xml`, `unique`, and `serialNumber` — those MIRROR fields from `frame_config.json`, they are not a second source. The agent never reads them back.
5. `reconcileMeurals` now has a per-productKey failure back-off (3 failures → 15-min skip) as defense-in-depth. Regardless of identity-file bugs, the server will not be flooded again.
6. File writes use `atomicWrite` (write-to-.tmp → fsync → rename → fsync-dir). A `.backup` copy is written after every successful primary write. Torn writes and SD-card power-loss corruption are now survivable.

## If you find yourself about to add a new .json to meurals/{uuid}/

Stop. Add the field to `frame_config.json`. Update `spec:bridge-per-meural-persistence`. If Java needs a different format (like XML for HWconfig), write a MIRROR file, not a new source. The mirror is never read back by the agent.
